description.p: This page lists the diagnostic identifiers reported by checkcode, codeIssues, and nelson-lint.
Each identifier is stable and can be used in configuration files or in local suppressions such as %#ok<NLS0004>.

tr.td: Syntax, lexical, input, or read error. The source file cannot be parsed or cannot be read.
The main function or class name differs from the source file name.
Code after return, break, or continue is unreachable in the current block.

A local variable is assigned but is never used afterwards. The analyzer ignores text inside comments and character vectors, does not count the left side of an assignment as a use, and skips this rule when dynamic assignment patterns make the local dataflow ambiguous.
A local variable is used before its first local assignment in a conservative, simple dataflow case.
A declared output argument is not assigned by the function body.
An input argument is never used by the function body.
A block is empty in a way that is likely accidental.
A condition is a trivial constant value such as true, false, 1, or 0.
A line ends with trailing whitespace. This diagnostic is trivially fixable.
The file does not end with a newline. This diagnostic is trivially fixable.
A line is longer than the configured maximum length.
A forbidden project term appears in source or help text.
Cyclomatic complexity is above the configured threshold.
Modified cyclomatic complexity is above the configured threshold.
The source line contains an invisible directional formatting character.
An output display call wraps sprintf. Prefer direct formatted output for clearer code.
A diagnostic call wraps sprintf. Prefer passing formatted arguments directly.
The code analyzer configuration file is invalid.
A file is longer than the configured maximum number of lines.
A function is longer than the configured maximum number of lines.
A dynamic code call or unsafe workspace mutation call is used. Simple command-form load calls can expose an unsafe suggestion to capture loaded data in a struct.
A local function is never called inside its file.
A local variable shadows a local function in the same file.
A floating-point literal is compared with exact equality.
Cognitive complexity is above the configured threshold.
A public function or class has no help comment. This diagnostic can insert a help comment skeleton.
A nested function variable shadows a symbol from a parent scope.
A local variable shadows an imported symbol.
An imported symbol is never used.
A class property is declared more than once in the same class.
A class method is declared more than once in the same class.
A class event is declared more than once in the same class.
A local variable or argument shadows a builtin function name.
A method variable or argument shadows a class property name.
A local assignment shadows an input argument name.
A class superclass is listed more than once in the same class.
A class attribute is listed more than once in the same class.

description.p: Rule levels can be changed with the rules object in nelson-lint.json. Version 2 configuration files must declare "version": 2. Accepted levels are allow, info, warning, and error.

example_item.example_item_description: Suppress an intentionally unused local variable.
